title: Estimates, Actual Cash Value and Total Loss Declaration
content:
**Rule.**
- Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), each estimate or supplement records three figures: the cumulative repair estimate, the actual cash value set by the package's valuation method, and the salvage bid.
- A vehicle is declared a total loss only when the latest estimate meets the garaging state's total loss test.
- An unrecovered stolen vehicle is declared a total loss at the end of the theft waiting period.
- A vehicle that is not a total loss is repaired, and each supplement is recorded with the next estimate sequence.

The total loss test is the one listed for the garaging state of the owner term in the company settlement schedule. It is applied to the figures of the latest estimate on the claim.

### Input, test and result (hypothetical)

| Latest estimate | Garaging state test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Repair 7,700.00; actual cash value 9,500.00 | Repair estimate at least 80 percent of the actual cash value (7,600.00) | Total loss |
| Repair 7,100.00; actual cash value 9,500.00 | Repair estimate at least 75 percent of the actual cash value (7,125.00) | Repaired, not a total loss |
| Repair 5,400.00; salvage 1,900.00; actual cash value 7,250.00 | Repair estimate plus salvage at least the actual cash value (7,300.00 against 7,250.00) | Total loss |

A second supplement after estimate sequence 2 is recorded as estimate sequence 3.
